BMD values are significantly higher in males than females; males exhibit higher peak bone mass than females, and attain this peak at an earlier age; females attain a peak BMD at around age 9 years, and BMD declines thereafter, whereas males attain a peak BDM at around age 7, and BMD is constant thereafter; and BMD as measured with DEXA is an imperfect predictor of vertebral fracture risk.
